name: Malva Pudding
summary: A spongy apricot-jam pudding soaked in hot cream sauce while still warm, served with custard or ice cream.
story: Malva pudding is a much-loved South African dessert of Cape Dutch origin, often served at family gatherings and in restaurants alike. Its sponge is light and caramelised on top, then soaked in a buttery cream sauce until it turns sticky and tender. Custard is the classic partner.

steps.title: Prepare the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180 C and grease a 23 cm baking dish, about 6 cm deep, with butter.

steps.title: Whisk eggs and sugar
steps.text: Beat the eggs and sugar for 4 to 5 minutes with an electric whisk until pale, thick and doubled in volume. Beat in the apricot jam until blended.

steps.title: Mix the dry
steps.text: Sift the flour, bicarbonate and salt together. In a jug, mix the melted butter, vinegar and milk.

steps.title: Fold the batter
steps.text: Fold the dry ingredients and the milk mixture into the eggs alternately, in two or three additions, until just combined. Stop as soon as no flour shows, or the sponge will be tough.

steps.title: Bake the sponge
steps.text: Pour into the dish and bake 30 to 35 minutes. It is done when deeply golden brown, risen, and a skewer in the centre comes out clean.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: While it bakes, warm the cream, butter, sugar, hot water and vanilla in a pan over low heat, stirring until the butter melts and the sugar dissolves. Do not boil.

steps.title: Soak the pudding
steps.text: As soon as the pudding leaves the oven, prick it all over with a skewer and slowly pour over the hot sauce. It will look like too much but the sponge absorbs it in 10 minutes.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Leave to stand 10 minutes more so the sauce settles. Serve warm in squares with hot custard, cream or vanilla ice cream.

tips: Pour the sauce over the pudding while both are hot; cold sponge soaks up the sauce badly.
Use plenty of skewer holes so the sauce reaches the bottom layer.
It reheats well in a low oven or the microwave.
Whisking eggs and sugar until pale is what gives the sponge its light texture.

swaps.swap: Use any smooth, tangy jam such as peach; avoid jams with large chunks.
Evaporated milk gives a slightly lighter sauce; the sponge stays moist.
Use fine white sugar, or part soft brown sugar for a deeper caramel flavour.
